sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: NOT MEASURED explicitly in the cited clip; the HA-tagged construct was used for characterization of WT and truncation mutant, implying the tagged protein was expressed and detectable, but no surface flow cytometry or IL-17 signaling assay result is reported in the ledger clip.
sites.rationale: IL17RA is a type I transmembrane receptor (signal peptide 1–32, ectodomain 33–320, TM 321–341, intracellular 342–866). The only extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 33; a tag placed before residue 33 would be inside the signal peptide and cleaved. Python-verified: residue 32 = S (last SP residue), residue 33 = L (first mature ectodomain residue). The junction 32|33 is 288 residues from the TM boundary, providing ample space. Four independent papers (L1–L4) all report N-terminal-tagged full-length IL17RA constructs expressed in mammalian cells, converging on this single extracellular terminus; L1 is cited as primary (HA tag, functional context), L2–L4 corroborate with Flag tag. Full-length human IL17RA with an N-terminal HA tag (IL17RA-HA construct) was expressed in cells and used to characterize wild-type receptor and the Y391* truncation mutant (PMC11796622). The same N-terminal position is independently corroborated by three additional reports of Flag-IL-17RA stable HEK293 lines used to study protein stability/degradation and receptor phosphorylation (PMC11047997; PMC13576895 x2). No residue number is stated in any clip; the junction is derived from topology: IL17RA is a type I single-pass receptor with signal peptide 1–32 and mature ectodomain beginning at residue 33. An N-terminal tag must be placed after SP cleavage (after residue 32) to reside on the extracellular face; upstream of residue 33 is cleaved off with the signal peptide.

sources.claim: Using skin cDNA from a healthy control individual, expression vectors were constructed for an N-terminal HA-tagged IL17RA (IL17RA-HA), IL17RA-Y391*-HA, and Il17RC-FLag.

literature_notes: L2, L3, and L4 all describe Flag-IL-17RA constructs at the same N-terminal junction (insert_after_residue=32) as L1; because they pin the same junction they corroborate site 1 rather than constituting separate sites. L5 (mouse IL-17RA-tTA) describes a C-terminal fusion; the C-terminus of IL17RA is intracellular (residues 342–866), so this is not a surface-tag site and is recorded in other_positions. No internal extracellular loop insertions are supported by any ledger line.

literature_other_positions.note: Mouse IL-17RA-tTA C-terminal fusion expressed on NIH-3T3 cells and shown to recruit IL-17RC-TEV upon cytokine binding; the C-terminus of IL17RA (residue 866, intracellular domain 342–866) faces the cytoplasm, making this an intracellular fusion, not a surface tag.
